<details class="project card-purple" id="cmdf">
<summary><span class="ptitle">The Daily Grind (CMD-F 2025)</span><span class="pitch">Built a conversation-starter web app in 24 hours that won the Social track and placed 3rd overall out of 50+ projects.</span><span class="ptags"><span class="tag tag-purple">Hackathon</span> <span class="tag tag-purple">Team project</span></span></summary>

<details class="project card-purple" id="datafest">
<summary><span class="ptitle">DataFest Statistical Analysis (ASA 2025)</span><span class="pitch">A fully reproducible 48-hour analysis with a Bayesian model, delivered with a dashboard, demo video and slides, all in Quarto.</span><span class="ptags"><span class="tag tag-green">Bayesian modelling</span> <span class="tag tag-green">EDA</span> <span class="tag tag-purple">Hackathon</span></span></summary>

A 48-hour [American Statistical Association DataFest](https://ww2.amstat.org/education/datafest/){target="_blank"} project with a team of 3. We built a fully reproducible analysis with extensive EDA and a Bayesian model, and delivered a dashboard, demo video and presentation slides, all made with Quarto.

[Presentation](https://hlan22.github.io/asa_datafest_2025/#/title-slide){target="_blank"} · [Repository](https://github.com/hlan22/asa_datafest_2025){target="_blank"}
</details>

<details class="project card-green" id="capstone">
<summary><span class="ptitle">Statistical Research Consulting (Capstone)</span><span class="pitch">Real client work in medical research: analyzed glaucoma surgery outcomes in R, presented at a poster session and to the client.</span><span class="ptags"><span class="tag tag-green">Statistics</span> <span class="tag tag-green">R</span> <span class="tag tag-green">Consulting</span></span></summary>

Real consulting work for a client in medical research, analyzing changes after glaucoma eye surgery (STAT 450).

- Presented regularly to Professor Rodolfo Lourenzutti to keep the work reliable.
- Met with the client, presented findings at a poster session, and gave technical oral presentations.
- Produced written reports, a code repository and visualizations in R and GitHub.
- Learned a lot about study design, model selection and communicating statistics.

![Our final poster board](../outputs/microshunt_poster_board.png){.lightbox}
</details>

<details class="project card-blue" id="reproducible">
<summary><span class="ptitle">Reproducible Software and CI/CD (DSCI 310)</span><span class="pitch">An R package plus an automated analysis pipeline using Docker, GNU Make and GitHub Actions, with tests and documentation.</span><span class="ptags"><span class="tag tag-blue">R package</span> <span class="tag tag-blue">Docker</span> <span class="tag tag-blue">GitHub Actions</span></span></summary>

A group project to build a data analysis and a package that are fully reproducible:

- A documented, modular R package and scripts
- An analysis pipeline automated with GNU Make
- A reproducible report in R Markdown and Quarto
- A containerized environment shared through Docker
- Automated tests, documentation and deployment

[![Preview of the package repository](../outputs/drugage_package_image.png)](https://github.com/DSCI-310-2025/pkg.drugage){target="_blank"}

[Package repository](https://github.com/DSCI-310-2025/pkg.drugage){target="_blank"} · [Analysis repository](https://github.com/DSCI-310-2025/dsci-310-group-7-data-dudes){target="_blank"}
</details>

<details class="project card-purple" id="research">
<summary><span class="ptitle">Weather Extremes Research</span><span class="pitch">Summer research assistantship (URSA NSERC) using time series analysis in Python and R to find patterns in Canadian floods, droughts and wildfires.</span><span class="ptags"><span class="tag tag-purple">Research</span> <span class="tag tag-purple">Time series</span> <span class="tag tag-purple">Python</span></span></summary>

Research assistant at UBC in summer 2024 under a URSA NSERC scholarship, working with Professors Harry Joe and Natalia Nolde. I explored Canadian weather data on floods, droughts and wildfires to find patterns, using EDA and time series analysis, and presented my work weekly. I'm cleaning up the code to publish it in a public repository.
</details>

<details class="project card-green" id="dashboard">
<summary><span class="ptitle">Library Attendance Dashboard (DSCI 320)</span><span class="pitch">An interactive Python dashboard on San Francisco library attendance, built with two teammates to answer four research questions.</span><span class="ptags"><span class="tag tag-green">Python</span> <span class="tag tag-green">Data visualization</span></span></summary>

<details class="project card-blue" id="word">
<summary><span class="ptitle">wordplayr, an R package</span><span class="pitch">A documented R package with a vignette and a pkgdown website that finds patterns in word lists.</span><span class="ptags"><span class="tag tag-blue">R package</span> <span class="tag tag-blue">Roxygen</span> <span class="tag tag-blue">pkgdown</span></span></summary>

`wordplayr` finds patterns in a list of words: average word length, common starting letters, frequent vowel sounds and more. It has a README with install instructions, a vignette, a package website and Roxygen documentation. I built it to learn why I like my favorite words (they most often start with "C").

[![Preview of the package website](../outputs/wordplay_website.png)](https://hlan22.github.io/wordplay/){target="_blank"}

[Repository](https://github.com/hlan22/wordplay){target="_blank"} · [Website](https://hlan22.github.io/wordplay/){target="_blank"}
</details>

<details class="project card-blue" id="easy">
<summary><span class="ptitle">easyEDA, a Python package (in progress)</span><span class="pitch">A Python package that automates exploratory data analysis by choosing the right plot for each column's data type.</span><span class="ptags"><span class="tag tag-blue">Python package</span> <span class="tag tag-blue">EDA</span></span></summary>

A package that automates EDA for any dataset by picking suitable plots for each column's data type. It supports quick exploration and presentation-ready, interactive visuals, and I plan to add an R version.

[Repository](https://github.com/hlan22/easy_eda){target="_blank"}
</details>
